# SK1035 — Use `Enum.GetValues<T>()`

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`Enum.GetValues(typeof(T))` returns `Array`; the generic overload returns `T[]`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.6 |

## Why

The non-generic overload returns `System.Array`, so every caller casts or enumerates as `object` and boxes each member. The generic overload is typed and allocation-free per element, and it is the same call.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
foreach (TokenKind kind in Enum.GetValues(typeof(TokenKind))) {
}
```

Write:

```csharp
foreach (var kind in Enum.GetValues<TokenKind>()) {
}
```

## When it does not fire

Requires the generic `System.Enum.GetValues<T>()` to exist in the compilation, and requires the argument to be a `typeof` naming a type the semantic model resolves to an enum. A `typeof` over a type parameter, over a non-enum, or over anything the model cannot resolve is silent, and so is a call to a user-declared type that happens to be named `Enum`. ⚠ **#425: the position is proved, not assumed.** The loop variable's type is the collection's element type, `object` over `Array` and the enum over `T[]`, so `foreach (var v in …)` changed overloads and `v = "x"` became CS0029, and `foreach (long n in …)` unboxed (`InvalidCastException`) where it now converts — all measured by #412's audit. A loop variable must be written as the enum or as `object`, a deconstructing `foreach` is declined, and a member access must bind, with the generic call in its place, to exactly the same member. With that, and every executable fixture's `Probe` unchanged, the fix is safe again.
